corrected_answer: Treat this as provisional RoCE performance guidance, not a platform diagnosis. Assume a multi-node GPU collective but verify GPU-direct versus host staging, transport selection, topology, PCIe/NVLink affinity, firmware, drivers, library, MTU, link speed, VLAN/priority mapping, routes, queue-pair count, message sizes, concurrency, and clock alignment. Hypothesis: tail instability is caused by a path or lossless-priority mismatch or congestion, rather than workload drift. Capture per-collective p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency in ms, throughput, retries/timeouts, completion errors, NIC drops/ECN and switch PFC/queue counters; correlate synchronized application, NIC, and switch timestamps and inspect verbs work requests/completions and buffer registration. Interleave fixed-placement baseline and treatment runs with equal sample counts and report confidence intervals. First collect read-only evidence; only then use a one-variable reversible canary. Abort and restore the last known-good configuration if p99.9 worsens by a predeclared threshold, correctness fails, or timeout/drop/PFC counters rise. Do not claim improvement without matched workload evidence.
